ingredientSections.heading: Fish Stock
items: 1kg fish frames (bones) -Save them up in the freezer or ask your fishmonger
¼ Cup parsley, leaves and stems

ingredientSections.heading: Shrimp Bisque
items: Heads & shells 15 large tiger prawns (from the Cioppino recipe)

ingredientSections.heading: Cioppino
items: 15 large tiger prawns, remove and reserve heads and shells for the Shrimp Bisque
300ml Sicilian tomato sauce or similar pasta sauce

methodSections.heading: Fish Stock
steps: Rinse the fish frames of any blood. Cut the vegetables into rough chunks.
Gently sauté the vegetables in olive oil or butter until soft without browning. Add all the remaining ingredients and cover with water.
Bring to a boil and then simmer for 30 minutes. Carefully skim off any foam that comes to the surface.
Strain through a fine mesh strainer. Season with salt and pepper. Stock can be stored in the fridge for a few days or frozen.

methodSections.heading: Shrimp Bisque
steps: Sauté the heads and shells of the tiger prawns from the Cioppino recipe over a medium heat with the roughly chopped vegetables in olive oil or butter until they start to caramelize.
Add the tomato paste and stir thoroughly so it coats everything and browns further.

Cover with fish stock and deglaze the bottom of the pot. Bring to a boil and then reduce the heat to a slow simmer. Simmer for several hours covered with a lid and top up with water or more fish stock as necessary.
Strain through a fine mesh sieve reserving the liquid. Add the cream and season with salt and pepper.

methodSections.heading: Cioppino
steps: Finely chop the garlic and sauté it in a large frying pan with the olive oil and carrot. Add all the seafood except the baby shrimp and scallops. Add the chili flakes and oregano.

When the seafood is cooked all the way through, deglaze the pan with the white wine. Add the tomato sauce, shrimp bisque, peas, and spinach, stir together and bring to a boil. Add the fish stock and bring back to a boil.
Add the baby shrimp and scallops and let simmer for 3-4 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve in a large bowl with a side of good bread and garnish with fresh parsley.
